Data Engineer Internship
Five positions available | University of Sydney students | Third and fourth year

Organisation: Yooamigo Pty Ltd

Location: Remote
Duration and hours: To be discussed
Commencement: November 2026
Remuneration: Unpaid
PEP recognition: Subject to University of Sydney approval and individual PEP requirements
Applications close: 11 December 2026

About the opportunity:
Help turn fragmented information into datasets that people can use to understand the world around them.

Yooamigo Pty Ltd is developing a geospatial intelligence platform bringing together data on infrastructure, property, energy, transport and the environment through interactive maps and 3D visualisation.

We are seeking five motivated third- and fourth-year University of Sydney students for supervised Data Engineer Internships. These roles offer practical experience in coding, data extraction, data quality and the development of documented, reproducible datasets. They are intended for students seeking relevant professional experience and, where approved, hours towards the Professional Engagement Program.

What you will work on:
- Working on a defined project suited to your skills and interests, you will:
- Identify and assess relevant public or appropriately licensed data sources.
- Develop Python scripts to collect information through APIs, MCPs, downloads and permitted extraction methods.
- Clean, standardise and combine datasets from different sources.
- Develop checks for missing information, duplicates, inconsistent records and geographic accuracy.
- Support geocoding and the preparation of datasets for mapping and spatial analysis.
- Document data provenance, collection methods, limitations and permitted uses.
- Use version control and contribute to code reviews, progress discussions and technical documentation.
- Prepare a final datasets, reproducible workflow and project report or presentation.

Projects may involve energy demand, infrastructure developments, transport, property or environmental information.

Who should apply:
These roles suit third- and fourth-year students studying software engineering, computer engineering, electrical engineering or related disciplines with a strong interest in data.

You should have:
- Working knowledge of Python, or similar languages, database experience, and an interest in solving practical data problems.
- Familiarity with CSV, JSON, spreadsheets or databases.
- Careful attention to data quality and documentation.
- The ability to communicate clearly, seek guidance and work reliably.
- Experience with SQL, pandas, Git, APIs, GIS or geospatial formats is desirable. You do not need experience with every tool.

Learning and research opportunities:
You will gain experience developing data workflows for an emerging technology platform, with supervision from Dr Milinda Suraweera and other professional engineers. The placement will include agreed learning objectives, regular feedback and support for documenting your experience.

Where the work produces a suitable original contribution, there may be opportunities to contribute to research papers, dataset publications or journal articles. Publication and authorship will depend on contribution, research quality, permissions and editorial review; publication is not guaranteed.

Email your CV, links to coursework and GitHub repos if available, and a short statement outlining your interests, relevant coding or data experience, availability and PEP requirements to:
